title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Samir Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost across hosted and dedicated deployments by providing an automated defaults layer for batching and KV-prefix caching, expose quantization profile recommendations for model variants, and add unit-economics tooling in Console/API so teams can see estimated $/request before rollout. This PR implements a first-pass autotune service (server-side) that observes live request distributions and suggests defaults, integrates quant profiles into the model catalog and serving runtime, and surfaces per-route cost estimates in the Console.

What changed (high level):
- New autotune service (serving/autotune) that evaluates latency and token distribution to recommend batch/window defaults and cache policies.
- Updated serving runtime to accept autotune recommendations and fall back safely (runtime can be toggled via env).
- Quantization profile plumbing: model registry + runtime selection of recommended quant profile per workload.
- Unit-economics API + Console panel that computes estimated $/request using tokens, batch size, and model profile.
- Tests and telemetry: added e2e tests for autotune flow and metrics/hooks to verify recommendations impact.

Checklist:
- [x] Autotune service + API endpoints
- [x] Runtime integration and safe fallback paths
- [x] Model catalog quant profile metadata + selection logic
- [x] Console UI (Unit Economics panel) and API route
- [x] Telemetry and e2e tests
- [x] Docs: docs/cost-optimization/autotune.md

Notes on safety and rollout: autotune recommendations are advisory by default and can be applied via per-route settings in the Console. Runtime will only apply autotune rules automatically for customers who opt-in. Quant profile selection is conservative: we only recommend quant levels that passed quality thresholds in evals.

Backwards compatibility: no breaking changes to public API. Autotune endpoints are behind feature flag and require RBAC to apply recommendations.

Related: ENG-1982, PM-874.

review_comments: Aisha Khan: Overall looks good. Main concern is safety — can we ensure recommendations have an opt-in flag and a visible audit trail?
Samir Patel: Yes, recommendations are advisory by default and require opt-in to apply. We added audit logs and a per-route history in Console.
Marco Diaz: Need benchmarks showing tail latency impact when autotune recommends larger batch sizes. Can you add worst-case percentile graphs?
Samir Patel: Added 99th/95th percentile telemetry to the autotune dashboard and included a short benchmark in tests/e2e.
Evelyn Wu: Quant profiles look good but add a guard to avoid recommending >2-bit quant for models with eval regression >0.5%
Samir Patel: Added a conservative quality threshold check and unit tests for quant profile selection.
release_notes: Adds an advisory autotune service for batching and caching defaults, quantization profile recommendations in the model catalog, and a Unit Economics panel in Console that shows estimated $/request. Autotune is opt-in and recommendations are auditable.
